title: Stop YouTube recommending things
summary: Pause your watch history and the home page stops trying to guess what you want.
changes: The home page empties out and stops recommending. Subscriptions, search and playlists keep working exactly as before.
steps: Open the link and choose "Turn off" under YouTube History.
Optionally delete what is already there, or set automatic deletion after 3 months.
Return to YouTube. The home page is now blank, with a note explaining why.
how: YouTube's recommendations are built almost entirely from watch history. Remove the input and the output stops.
caveats: You lose "continue watching" and your viewing history list.
Some people find the empty home page liberating and others find it disorienting. It is reversible in one tap.

alternatives.label: Keep history but watch only subscriptions

title: Open YouTube on your subscriptions
summary: Bookmark the subscriptions page and never see the recommendation engine again.
changes: You see new videos from channels you chose, in date order. Nothing is suggested.
how: The subscriptions feed is a straightforward chronological list. It is the only part of YouTube that does exactly what you asked it to.
steps: Open the link above and bookmark it, or add it to your phone's home screen so it opens like an app.
On iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen. On Android: menu → Add to Home screen.
caveats: The mobile app always opens on Home. The home-screen shortcut opens the website instead, which is the point.
Keeping your subscription list tidy matters more once this is your main view.

title: Teach YouTube to stop suggesting something
summary: "Not interested" and "Don't recommend channel" genuinely work, if you use them consistently.
changes: Specific videos and whole channels stop appearing in your recommendations.
steps: Tap the three dots on any recommended video.
Choose "Not interested", or better, "Don't recommend channel".
To undo past damage, open your history and remove individual videos that sent the algorithm astray.
how: These signals are weighted heavily. Channel-level blocking is far stronger than per-video dismissal, and persists.
caveats: It only affects the account you are signed into on that profile.
Watching even a few seconds of something is a stronger positive signal than "not interested" is a negative one.

sources.title: Manage your recommendations and search results (official)

title: Turn off the Shorts feed
summary: The endless vertical feed can be collapsed, hidden, or time-limited.
changes: Shorts stop appearing on the home page and the Shorts tab disappears or is limited.
steps: In the app: Settings → General → Manage all history, or Settings → Time management.
Look for the Shorts limit and set it, which hides the feed for the chosen period.
On the home page: tap the three dots on a Shorts shelf and choose "Not interested" — it hides that shelf for 30 days.
On desktop, the Unhook add-on removes Shorts and much else permanently.
caveats: YouTube keeps moving this setting and the 30-day hide expires.
The desktop add-on is the only permanent removal.

title: Strip YouTube down to what you asked for
summary: An add-on that lets you remove the recommendation sidebar, the home feed, Shorts and comments.
changes: YouTube becomes a video player with a search box. You choose which parts return.
how: The add-on hides page elements in your browser. YouTube's servers are unaffected, so nothing about your account changes.
caveats: Desktop and Firefox for Android only.
YouTube redesigns break these add-ons from time to time; the popular ones are usually patched within days.

title: Stop others remixing your videos with AI
summary: If you post to YouTube, you can prevent your Shorts being used as raw material for generated remixes.
changes: Your videos can no longer be fed into YouTube's generative remix tools by other users.
steps: Open YouTube Studio and go to the Shorts section of Content.
Choose "Allow only audio remixing", or turn remixing off entirely.
Set it for existing videos as well as new uploads; it is per-video.
caveats: There is no single account-wide switch yet, which makes this tedious for large channels.
Rolled out gradually; not every account sees it.

title: Filter AI-generated music out
summary: Deezer is the only major streaming service that lets you hide fully AI-generated tracks.
changes: Tracks Deezer identifies as fully machine-generated are labelled, excluded from editorial playlists and can be filtered from recommendations.
how: Deezer built a detector for the signatures left by the common music generators, and made the results visible to listeners rather than keeping them internal. Tagged tracks are excluded from editorial and algorithmic recommendation.
caveats: Detection catches fully generated tracks, not songs where a person used AI tools as part of their process.
Requires a Deezer account; a free tier exists.
Spotify labels some AI accounts but offers no listener-facing filter.

sources.title: Deezer AI music tagging and detection

title: Buy music from the people who made it
summary: A shop where musicians upload their own work, write their own notes and are paid directly.
changes: You buy a file you keep, from an artist who receives most of the money.
how: Bandcamp pages are made by the artists themselves. There is no recommendation engine pushing you anywhere, and the editorial writing is done by human critics.
caveats: Generated music does exist on Bandcamp; the artist page usually makes the difference obvious.
Not a streaming replacement — it is a shop and a discovery tool.

title: Let a human choose the music
summary: Stations where a person picks the records and tells you what they are.
changes: You hear a sequence someone thought about, with context, and you discover things no engine would have offered you.
how: Community and public stations run on human programming by constitution. Radio Garden lets you spin a globe and listen to any of them.
caveats: You cannot skip tracks. That is the arrangement, and much of the pleasure.

title: Stop the next thing starting by itself
summary: Turn off autoplay previews and next-episode autoplay, per profile.
changes: Nothing moves or plays until you ask it to. Browsing becomes quiet.
steps: Open your Netflix account page on the website — the setting does not exist in the mobile app.
Choose a profile, then Playback settings.
Uncheck both autoplay options. Repeat for each profile.
caveats: Per profile, not per account.
Other services bury the equivalent setting in different places; look under Playback or Accessibility.
